caption: The drawing is a technical plan of a chair and appears to be executed in pencil or ink on a lightly yellowed or off-white paper. It features three main views: at the top left is a plan view showing the top-down layout of the seat and the stretcher supports, with clear rectangular and turned elements, and dimensions labeled in inches. Below this is a front view of the chair, displaying a rectangular seat and an upholstered back with vertical lines of tacks or fasteners, supported by turned front legs and plain back legs, with horizontal stretchers connecting the legs. To the right of the front view is a side view, which illustrates the gentle backward curve of the chair’s backrest, the rectangular profile of the seat, the placement of the stretchers, and shows the decorative turning on the front legs as well as the straight back legs. The drawing also includes a scale in inches near the upper right, and a rectangular title box indicating the chair is from the Sewall House in Secretary, Maryland, and that the drawing is for the Brooklyn Museum, with a reference number at the top right. All measurements, labels, and structural features are meticulously detailed with straight and dashed lines.
title: Side Chair
